body: TSMC, the juggernaut that produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips, has discovered a data leak said to contain over 46,000 employee records, according to Seeking Alpha . The company made a Form 6-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, stating: "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised." The company says the info has been verified to match data "stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," although said provider is not named. TSMC says it has informed those impacted by the breach and is providing support, and has also engaged with the cloud service vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to "ascertain the facts and take necessary actions." body: Intel appears to have gained market share from AMD in a rare turnaround for the company. The red team's chips have been in the lead in performance and popularity for many years now, and frankly, they still are. That's what weird about this one: AMD may have lost ground because it makes the best CPUs for gaming . The latest Q3, 2026 data from market researchers Mercury Research suggests an increase in market share for desktop CPUs of 5.1%. Now, considering AMD has fought tooth and nail for a decade to increase its share to around 35% as of Q2, 2026, dropping down to just 29.9% in the following three months marks a gargantuan lurch back towards Intel. Our pick for the best gaming CPU is the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , and many other AMD chips make up our recommendations. While we do recommend the Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus due to its surprisingly low price tag and plenty of cores, I wouldn't go as far as believing any Arrow Lake chip has been key to turning around Intel's fortunes among gamers. title: Reddit tells me it’s not going to make a penny in affiliates from Reddit Reviews and is working hard to avoid inauthentic content
summary: "Reddit does not receive a cut of any purchases made through the buy it now button on product pages."
body: A couple of days ago I reported that Reddit is rolling out reviews for different products, informed by Redditors' thoughts and molded by AI into into dedicated review pages for these products. Given Reddit says "many reviews also include images, prices, and purchase links", I wondered whether Reddit would be making any affiliate money from this. Well, I now have an answer: the company tells us it will not receive a cut. In an email sent to me, a Reddit rep explains: "Reddit Reviews is an organic experience, and Reddit does not receive a cut of any purchases made through the buy it now button on product pages." Not that I would have had a massive problem with this—PC Gamer earns affiliate revenue itself—but I suppose it's good to know there won't be a financial incentive there at least in that respect. And it does at least tie in with the aimed "organic" nature of Reddit in general. I was also concerned that users might review-bomb products they don't like, or that companies could use bots to positively influence reviews for their own products. title: 'Heist of a new kind': AI-enabled scam reportedly managed to steal $110 million from French bank
summary: That's reportedly one quarter's profits for the bank.
body: AI-enabled hacking is only continuing to get more impressive, and more scary, as a French bank claims a hacking group has cost it €100,000,000 (around $110,000,000)—about one quarter's profits. So not much, then? That's according to an interview with Julien Carmona of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa with the AFP , which Boursorama reported. Carmona detailed the hack in an interview, claiming it to be a "heist of a new kind", stating the company has the "dubious honor of being the first French bank, and I believe the first European bank, to be the target of a successful fraudulent attack." (machine translated). Carmona says the hack is "unprecedented in terms of sophistication" and "technicality". Effectively, the hacking group managed to create fake IBANs, including those from Fortuneo (a bank owned by the group), "to trigger payment orders from Crédit Mutuel Arkea's own account to external parties using instant payment systems". These, "by definition have fewer controls than on classic transfers." Carmona did clarify to Les Echos that though they use Fortuneo IBANs, "Fortuneo's system, and therefore its customers, were not affected." ‼️ AI-enabled hackers pulled about €100 million out of Fre…

title: Microsoft says there is 'no evidence of malicious activity' being the cause of the global service outage affecting governments and organisations around the world
summary: A bunch of governments, state institutions, and companies are affected globally.
body: Welcome to the new era, folks, where we increasingly seem to be heading closer to a daily coin flip over whether our core online services stay live or go down. This time, it's Microsoft. Down Detector reports problems with Microsoft 365 services since about 12:30 pm (ET) yesterday, November 12, and issues are still ongoing. Countries across the world are affected, and some institutions have been affected severely. Parts of the UK government, for instance, are having problems sending and receiving emails. The UK's health service, the NHS, has reportedly said it is unable to access online consultation for patients . The US and other governments have reportedly been impacted , too. Microsoft explains that certain features of services "that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted." So, it looks like Exchange Online could be the culprit. This is the back-end of Microsoft services that use calendars, tasks, emails, and so on. Affected services include MS365 admin center, apps, Education features, Copilot, Defender for Office 365, Defender XDR, Fabric, Graph, Intune, Planner, Power Apps, Purview, some elements of Teams, To Do, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and…

title: Xbox CEO looks to the future as Microsoft's console turns 25: 'A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations'
summary: Asha Sharma doesn't specifically mention AI in her 25th anniversary message, but I'm pretty sure that's what she's talking about.
body: In a message marking the 25th anniversary of the first Xbox console , Xbox CEO Asha Sharma predicts that the future of gaming will look much like its beginning, "when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays." And even though the term never actually appears in her post, yeah, I'm pretty sure she's talking about AI. Sharma's message kicks off with a blast from the early days of Microsoft, beginning with a look at Microsoft Adventure, an adaptation of Colossal Cave "that looked more like MS-DOS than an early version of Minecraft," and the first-ever Microsoft staff photo that showcases some absolutely spectacular hair. From there it's a quick trip through Microsoft Flight Simulator, Quake, DirectX, and then in 2001, the original Xbox. Naturally, there's a tribute to the "generations of employees, studios, developers, and partners" who helped create and grow Xbox, and the people who have played on various generations of consoles over the years. body: The dust hasn't even settled yet after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO , and the US government is already making it pretty clear where it stands on who gets the job next. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken up the role of CEO following Huang's departure, but only on an interim basis. The Nvidia board will have to decide on a full-time replacement to take over from Huang, who had led the company since its founding in 1993. The chairman of the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, John Moolenaar, has put out a statement on the high-profile departure. title: Jensen Huang leaving Nvidia is not a good thing for PC gaming, and I’ll tell you why
summary: We PC gamers are far from the belle of the AI ball.
body: Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as Nvidia CEO . That's such an odd sentence to write, as a huge part of my career as a tech journalist has revolved around covering Nvidia, its graphics cards, and its leather-jacketed chief. As I write this article, I'm already seeing reactions on social media from PC gamers. Some are shocked, some are indifferent, and some appear to be celebrating. In terms of the latter, I'd imagine that's because the ex-Nvidia boss has become one of the most recognisable figures behind the great AI revolution, which, err, isn't popular within our hobby, to say the least. Not only that, but RAM is ludicrously expensive, with storage not far behind. And graphics cards, Nvidia's gaming bread and butter? The price increases recently have been mind-boggling. All of these things are, in the main, AI server-demand induced, and Nvidia is behind the chips that power most of those servers, making vast amounts of money in the process. And so on that level, I can understand why some might cheer his departure, equating the company's figurehead with Nvidia's new place in the AI economy as a whole—leaving us gamers in the lurch. "I think that the folks at Infinity Ward probably thought I was a little crazy when I came in," Kurosaki tells us. title: Humble Bundle's new redesign inexplicably removes 2-factor authentication, dramatically weakening account security
summary: I recommend removing your saved payment details, at least for now.
body: Users of Humble Bundle —the pay-what-you-want game-bundle storefront that will also sell you books and software—have been alarmed by a new redesign that seems to have axed a foundational piece of login security tech. The just-released new Humble Bundle website has no support for two-factor authentication whatsoever: users are unable to add it to their accounts, while those who had previously set it up on the old site design (including yours truly) are able to log in with just an email and password. At no point in the login process does the site ask you to input a 2FA code. Humble Bundle does not address the removal of 2FA anywhere on its new site. In fact, the site's FAQs still feature articles encouraging users to make use of it to keep their accounts secure, which is currently impossible. I have reached out to Humble Bundle to ask if the change was intentional and if it will be reversed, and will update this piece if I hear back. This is, to put it mildly, concerning. The point of two-factor (or multi-factor) authentication is to make user accounts—which, on Humble Bundle, may well have credit card info saved to them—more secure. Even in the event your account password became co…

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly had a second affair with another Nvidia exec
summary: A new report says that video evidence of the affair exists, but was swept under the rug.
body: Days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy (China denies any espionage ), The New York Times has reported new claims that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him: Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia VP who oversees the company's healthcare tech-related efforts. NYT cites five sources who work at the company, and says that it is aware of, but has not seen, video evidence of the affair. It's a story you could see playing out in a film noir thriller. According to NYT's sources, Huang and Powell were seen "being affectionate" at a hotel in the vicinity of an Nvidia conference earlier this year. A bystander allegedly captured a video of the interaction, but according to the report was made an offer by security personnel—details unknown—in return for signing an NDA. Nvidia's board of directors is investigating the national security concerns raised by the affair Huang disclosed over the weekend, and The Wall Street Journal reported today that the board is preparing to oust the CEO. At the time of writing, the company has not commented on this new allegation. PC Gamer has reached out.

title: I have converted GTA 5 from crime sim to train sim
summary: Choo choo.
body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier . As we've already discussed, I regard the personal automobile as a vector of poisonous ideology . Its beneficent alternative? The train: socialised, communal, predictable, subject to the gentle yet firm hand of rational state planning. If the world had more trains in it, we wouldn't be where we are now. We'd be somewhere else. On account of catching the train. I have converted Grand Theft Auto 5's Franklin Clinton into one of the hero-drivers of these great iron beasts. I have installed Los Santos Metro Driver , which transforms Rockstar's opus from crime sim to train sim. Or tram sim, I guess. Same thing. The city's denizens need to move between airport terminals and only man can help them do it (you are that man). Did you know driving trains, like, sucks? It's hard. You'd think it'd be easy, what with being essentially glued to your surface of operation , but I have spent most of my career as a trainee train-er overshooting platf…
